title.value: What does it mean to be a responsible AI practitioner: An ontology of roles and skills
title.justification: The paper primarily focuses on defining roles and skills for AI practitioners involved in ethical AI practices.
title.quote: What does it mean to be a responsible AI practitioner: An ontology of roles and skills

extractions.description: The paper examines the roles and necessary skills for responsible AI practitioners or AI ethicists, who interpret and operationalize best ethical and safe design practices for AI systems. It proposes an ontology created through analysis of industry job postings and expert interviews, aiming to guide business leaders and educators in building AI ethics teams and curricula.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses responsible AI practices, it doesn't center around climate or ecological sustainable development. It predominantly focuses on the ethical and social aspects of AI deployment.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The so-called responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) practitioners or AI ethicists are generally tasked with interpreting and operationalizing best practices for ethical and safe design of AI systems.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on ethical and responsible AI practices rather than directly on climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: The purpose of this study is to examine the experiences of professionals including ethicists, technologists and business leaders who are dealing with ethical and social implications of particular AI technology.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address any climate or ecological sustainable development topics that fall into the predefined categories.
secondary_categories.quote: The emergence of these roles challenges technology companies to curate these roles and teams.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories are irrelevant as the paper does not address topics directly related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Companies and governmental organizations are paying more attention to the impact AI can have on our society and how AI systems should be designed and deployed responsibly.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As there are no applicable primary categories, sub-categories don't apply here either.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The new set of occupations has emerged in the industry focusing on ethical and social implications rather than environmental.

applications.justification: The paper does not provide specific applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: This work is more concerned with ethical frameworks and competencies within AI roles.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need for a new category, as the focus is not on climate or ecological sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: This ontology contributes to business leaders looking to build responsible AI teams and provides educators with a set of competencies that an AI ethics curriculum can prioritize.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no extension of current climate sub-categories needed as the focus is not related to those areas.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: As illustrated in Figure 1, our competency framework outlines seven occupations that responsible AI practitioners hold in the industry.
